figmaExecutionNotes: Use one master page with reusable section components and auto-layout wrappers for each section.
Maintain dark theme throughout with section-level tonal variation rather than switching to light backgrounds.
Keep hero and trust as the strongest first-fold sequence; do not introduce unsupported awards, testimonials, pricing, or forms.
Use Sora for headings and Inter for body copy across all sections to match marketing-product personality.

For mobile, stack hero content vertically, compress the logo strip into a horizontally scrollable row, convert both feature grids to single-column cards, and present the video gallery as stacked tiles or a swipeable list.
Preserve consistent padding tokens: 80px desktop section spacing, 48px mobile section spacing, with 24px container gutters.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro—built for professional image generation, video generation, and multimodal production workflows.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a dark premium split hero with the copy block on the left and a cinematic layered media stack on the right. The right side should combine a large product collage, a looping preview card for Seedance, and small glass UI cards showing prompt-to-output and high-resolution render states. Add orange edge glows, subtle grid lines, and floating metric chips to signal enterprise-grade creative AI. The hero should feel production-ready and inventive, with the orange CTA standing out strongly against charcoal surfaces.

repetitionBreakers: Use a split hero with cinematic media, then switch to a logos-first trust strip on a contrasting light surface.
Make the product section alternate between a preview-led tabs layout for Seedream and a split-panel video-first layout for Seedance.
Use a dark proof/testimonial carousel after bright product surfaces to reset visual energy.
Reserve the most aggressive CTA emphasis for the pricing and final lead-form sections only.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate professional AI images and videos with ByteDance models Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore how it works, see trusted proof, and get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark cinematic gradient with orange mesh glow and subtle waveform overlays
sections.designNote: Keep the hero content-first to satisfy continuity with the ad message. Headline must answer what this is; subheadline must clearly define the audience as creative teams and businesses; CTA must be a single solid orange button labeled 'Get started'. Right side should feel like a premium AI studio stack: prompt cards, image frames, video thumbnails, and audio-visual cues. Include banner chips for AI image generation, AI video generation with audio, multimodal content creation, and enterprise-ready infrastructure.

Place trust early because the traffic is warm and the proof type is logos. Since no logos are provided, use a metric-strip fallback styled as recognisable partner placeholders with brand-safe SVG treatment. Keep it compact and visually distinct from the hero by switching to a light band. If actual logos become available, convert this into a 3-6 logo strip. Avoid testimonials here.

Insert the required 3-step process section immediately after trust to match warm-traffic sequence. Use a concise, under-60-seconds structure: 1) describe the prompt or upload reference, 2) generate image/video outputs, 3) refine, sync, and export. Present as a visually paced split-panel sequence with one animated preview per step rather than a flat card grid. This section should feel fast and production-oriented.

Use a high-contrast light section and make Seedream the first product block because it is the click-driving image-generation promise. Since there are 5+ features, use tabs with a preview panel instead of a static grid. First block: Seedream 4.5 spotlight with tabs for alignment, resolution, typography, composition, and structural fidelity. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro should switch to a darker split-panel video-first layout with playback frames and motion cues, not the same pattern as Seedream. This alternating treatment prevents monotony and highlights the image-to-video breadth.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ testimonials. Make it feel like industry proof rather than generic praise: creative director, video producer, art director, marketing manager, creative lead. Use dark glass cards with orange quote marks and minimal chrome. Keep it concise and credibility-led, not salesy.

Dedicate one more section to the 1-2 features most tied to the click: Seedream text-image alignment and Seedance audio-visual synchronization. Use a spotlight-plus-grid format with a large lead visual and smaller supporting callouts, so the page does not fall into a generic feature dump. This section should feel more technical and product-confident, with comparison snippets, prompt/output examples, and a compact capability matrix.

Place pricing after proof and features to support decision-making. Use a two-card comparison with Seedance slightly emphasized for video-production buyers, but keep both cards clearly differentiated. Every CTA must still read 'Get started' and be filled orange at 100% opacity. No gray, no outline. Include the $1,000/month starting price for Seedance if shown, but keep the visual treatment premium and uncluttered.

Final conversion block should be the strongest CTA moment on a light surface for contrast. Keep it simple: one centered form or lead card, one primary button only, full-width on mobile, labeled 'Get started'. Reinforce 'See it in action' as the intent without changing the button text. Make this section feel like a polished handoff to sales or demo booking.

blueprint.designPersonality: A dark, premium, production-ready creative AI experience with orange-led accents, strong enterprise trust signals, and a polished video-first gallery that feels like a high-end generative studio for marketing and creative teams.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a cinematic right-side visual stack with floating model cards, orange glow edges, waveform overlays, prompt-to-output frames, and a gallery section featuring short video thumbnails with play icons. Add a dominant logo-proof band near the top with SVG logos in monochrome white/orange on dark surfaces. Supplement with abstract UI shells, metric chips, and glassmorphism panels rather than generic stock photography.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so it needs a smaller, premium-sized hero treatment to preserve balance on a dark visual-first layout.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette only provides orange, white, black, and light grey, so the entire system is built around a dark charcoal base with orange as the dominant action and emphasis colour.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen, left-aligned hero with strong H1, concise supporting copy, and one primary CTA. Brand/logo placement sits above or beside the headline area. Hero content is compact and product-led rather than story-led, with supporting bullets used to reinforce key value points.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero first, then a lead-capture/form section, followed by stacked product-detail sections. The page uses a linear, conversion-oriented flow with clear vertical separation between major blocks rather than a complex navigation structure.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple utility cards with clear borders or subtle elevation, generous internal padding, and minimal decoration. Content is structured for scanability, typically using a title, short description, and compact supporting bullets or feature rows.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is prominent and action-oriented in the hero; secondary CTAs are either absent or used sparingly in later product sections. CTA hierarchy favors one dominant conversion action per section, with form submission serving as the main conversion mechanism.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is surfaced in the reference pattern. If pricing is introduced, it should follow the same restrained, conversion-first layout with compact plan cards and strong hierarchy rather than a comparison-heavy table.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not evidenced in the provided reference pattern; assume a minimal utility footer or standard site footer outside the core landing-page experience.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Hero media is lightweight or absent; the page relies more on typography and structured content than large visual storytelling. Supporting imagery, if used, should be product-relevant and aligned to adjacent copy rather than full-bleed decorative art.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked content sections with repeated product blocks, each using a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and a list of key benefits. Sections should support progressive disclosure by grouping features into digestible clusters and keeping each block visually consistent.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead form is positioned early and treated as a major conversion module. The form uses a boxed card treatment with a headline, stacked fields, hidden metadata fields, and a compact interaction model optimized for quick submission.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-driven presentation with no visible motion system implied in the reference. Interaction should remain understated, prioritizing fast comprehension and form completion over animation.
designNotes: Favor a conversion-first landing page structure with minimal navigation complexity.
Use strong typographic hierarchy and concise feature lists to support fast scanning.
Keep section treatments consistent and modular so repeated product blocks feel like a system.
Reserve visual emphasis for the hero and form rather than decorative elements.
Design for B2B clarity: compact copy, direct CTAs, and structured benefit framing.

blueprint.additionalInstructions:
PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

use dark theme and a gallery section containing videos

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with bold product positioning and immediate AI capability clarity
Logo-first trust band placed high on the page to establish enterprise credibility
Split showcase for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with distinct image and video use cases
Video gallery section featuring motion examples, cinematic outputs, and audio-visual generation samples
Capability-led feature blocks highlighting image quality, multimodal editing, lip-sync, and speed
Proof-rich testimonial section emphasizing reduced turnaround time and easier evaluation
Clear demo or quote-oriented conversion points after each major product module
avoidPatterns: Avoid badge-heavy trust stacking without recognizable company logos
Avoid a long-form editorial intro that delays product understanding
Avoid generic stock imagery that weakens the AI product story
Avoid equal-weight treatment of both products in the hero; lead with the stronger acquisition message
Avoid too many competing CTAs above the fold
Avoid light, airy layouts that reduce the premium futuristic feel
Avoid feature dumps without visual proof or sample outputs
designStrategy.reasoning: This landing page should be optimized for demo booking because the audience is professional and business-focused, the product is complex and high-consideration, and the pricing signals imply an enterprise sales motion. The visitor is likely solution-aware, so the page should quickly validate capability, show tangible outputs, and move into proof and consultation. Because the brief explicitly says visitors trust logos most, trust should be structured around recognizable brand logo placement rather than testimonials or badges. A dark, futuristic visual system suits advanced generative AI and helps video/gallery content stand out. The hero should be immersive and product-led, with immediate proof of image and video generation value, followed by a gallery, feature explanation, and conversion prompts.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
